assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks (Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Sr lattice clock, Ye's realisation of record-stability and accuracy) turned atomic spectroscopy into a platform where measurement uncertainty is now near 1e-18. The concept is original, the physics is clean (Lamb-Dicke confinement with cancelled light shifts), and the impact spans time standards, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and prospects for redefining the second. This is the kind of measurement-limited advance I value most.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and made the first demonstrations; Ye drove the many-body, spin-polarised Sr clocks to the lowest systematic uncertainty. The credited list is exactly two, which gives a natural, uncontested two-person configuration, though others (for example Takamoto, Lemonde, Hall's frequency-comb work) contributed to the ecosystem.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several groups worldwide, with multiple species and a long record of improving accuracy. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely. Hall and Hänsch were already recognised in 2005 for the comb technology, so the lattice clock is a distinct step.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 and 2012 recognitions of frequency combs and ion-clock work could be argued to make this incremental.
I know Jun Ye's training in the Hall laboratory environment where I also spent time; I do not treat that as disqualifying but note it.
Not independently verified here: precise current clock uncertainty figures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable many-body quantum systems: the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, quantum gas microscopes and a general route to analogue quantum simulation. The originality (Jaksch-Zoller proposal followed by the Greiner-Bloch experiment) and breadth across condensed-matter models are very large.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied the decisive theoretical blueprint, Greiner and Bloch the first Mott-insulator experiment and subsequent microscope-scale control. Esslinger's fermionic work and Hänsch's role in the 2002 experiment complicate a three-person limit; I choose the theory-plus-experiment core.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended by many groups for more than twenty years, and increasingly used to address open questions. Recognition is timely, with the BEC prizes of 2001 only partly overlapping in subject.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is genuinely contested and any three-person split will omit someone significant.
Overlap with B009 (Zoller) and the 2001 BEC Nobel Prize.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered a decisive scientific discovery rather than a method is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution put the foundations of quantum mechanics (no-cloning, entanglement, Bell tests) to practical use and launched quantum communication as a field. BB84 and E91 are conceptually original, crisp and have had large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: BB84 is clearly Bennett and Brassard; E91 is Ekert's entanglement-based protocol. The three-name configuration is clean and compact, and the credited names cover the decisive contributors, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known historical complication.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated over fibre and satellite links by multiple groups, which also overlaps with the 2022 prize for entanglement tests and tends to complete the story. Recognition is not premature; the question is timeliness relative to the 2022 award.
uncertainties: Practical security (device imperfections, side channels) is still an active topic, so the application is mature but not closed.
Wiesner's priority claim and the role of the later experiments by others are not resolved in the supplied text.
Overlap with the 2022 prize may reduce urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault-tolerant, topological codes provide the conceptual basis for scalable quantum computing: the existence of error correction at all was far from obvious. The ideas are original and clear, and experiments now show error suppression below threshold in several platforms.
assessment.attribution: Shor's code and the fault-tolerance results, Steane's independently discovered code and Kitaev's topological codes are each decisive. The list leaves out Calderbank and Gottesman (and Aharonov, Ben-Or, Knill and others on threshold theorems), so the fair configuration is not self-evident.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstration of beyond-break-even and below-threshold logical qubits is recent and still platform-specific, so the full impact is arriving but not complete. Slightly early for a prize but not unreasonable.
uncertainties: Credit among Shor, Steane, Calderbank, Gottesman, Kitaev and the threshold-theorem authors is contested.
Experimental confirmation is recent and fast moving.
Shor's factoring algorithm is a distinct contribution not covered by this candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates and the Innsbruck experiments of Blatt (and the broader ion-qubit programme) established a leading quantum-computing and simulation platform with the highest gate fidelities. The importance and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the theoretical originators; Blatt led the key experimental implementations. Wineland and others were recognised in 2012, and Wineland's NIST work is not among the supplied names, which raises a legitimate question of whether this adds a distinct achievement.
assessment.maturity: Mature, independently reproduced in many labs and companies. Partial overlap with the 2012 Nobel Prize for control of individual quantum systems limits timeliness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with B044 and B015 where Zoller and Cirac recur.
Whether the ion-gate proposal is a sufficiently separate discovery from the Wineland-era control is arguable.
Credit for experimental gates is shared with NIST and Innsbruck colleagues not named here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED transferred cavity QED to superconducting circuits, giving strong coupling at microwave frequencies and the readout and coupling architecture of leading superconducting quantum processors. It is original, technically beautiful and has had large impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the architecture; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin is a credited theorist but I limit the list to three. The 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits touches the same community.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and now industrial. The 2025 award for circuit-based quantum phenomena reduces the near-term likelihood of another circuits prize and raises timing questions.
uncertainties: Overlap of community with the recent 2025 prize and 2012 cavity-QED prize.
Allocation among four credited names leaves Girvin out.
Impact is partly engineering of quantum computers rather than a new physical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry gives inertial and gravitational sensing with exceptional sensitivity, tests of the equivalence principle, measurements of G and alpha, and a prospective route to gravitational-wave detection. It directly embodies precision measurement via matter-wave interference.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated early matter-wave interferometers with gratings, Bordé gave the theory and the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer, Kasevich (with Chu) the light-pulse gyroscope and gravimeter. Steven Chu, Mlynek and others are not in the supplied names and the credit is fragmented.
assessment.maturity: Well established and replicated, but large-scale applications (fundamental-physics tests, field instruments) are still developing. Partly overlapping with the 1997 and 2001 prizes.
uncertainties: Fragmented attribution across many groups.
Overlap with the 1997 Chu prize on laser cooling and light-pulse methods.
Whether a single decisive discovery exists is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single NV centre spins in diamond opened solid-state quantum sensing of magnetic and electric fields, temperature and strain at the nanoscale, and a room-temperature spin-qubit platform. This is quantum sensing at the limits of what can be measured.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin is credited for later quantum-sensing and register work but is a second-wave contributor on this specific discovery. I keep the pair.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups confirm it and applications are broad, but the community consensus on a single decisive step is still forming and many applications are still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the strongest case is the single-spin demonstration or the sensing applications is open.
Lukin's role is not resolved in the supplied credit.
Applications in biology are less settled than the physics.
